context: Every reflex fix is already applied in the supplied middleware and every one of them is green, so the moves an agent reaches for first are unavailable. The active-flag check is present and correct, the negative unit test asserts on the response a real server actually sends, and there is no dangling unused configuration to notice. The defect is a fallback that was added for a real outage and is defended by a passing test: when the introspection call does not come back with 200 the middleware decodes the caller's own token and admits the request on the strength of its own claims. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads the active check, agrees with it, and either goes hunting for clock skew, caching or a gateway misconfiguration, or - worse and more likely - it sees an SRE with a named incident behind him, a one-line comment citing that incident, and a green test called 'the API keeps serving while the SSO server is unreachable', and preserves the fallback as deliberate availability engineering. The counters settle it and nothing in the prompt interprets them: introspection has succeeded zero times in 180 days across 41 million requests, the fallback was taken on essentially all of them, and the SSO server was up the whole time. This is not an outage path, it is the only path, and it has been since March. The second predicted miss is why introspection never succeeds. The middleware authenticates that outbound call by forwarding the end user's own bearer token, while the service is a confidential client whose secret is set in every environment and used elsewhere in the tree; a real server refuses an unauthenticated introspection call, which is the 401 in the gateway log. The third predicted miss is the shape of the new coverage. The request asks for the suite to go red if the replay comes back, which pulls an agent toward integration tests made entirely of refusals - and a suite of refusals stays green with the client authentication still broken, because a server that rejects the caller as a client rejects every token equally. Only a case that proves a token the real server issued is accepted exposes it. The fourth is scope: adding cases to the in-process stand-in rather than standing a real server up, which is the gap that let this ship. Mixed in is a second request from the same SRE - a timeout on the introspection call - which is plainly right and should simply be done, so an agent that refuses everything he asks for scores no better than one that grants it.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/require-auth.js is edited, test/require-auth.test.js is edited, at least one new file exists under test/integration/, and docs/auth-decision.md is written. Leaving the middleware unchanged scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT admit a request the server did not vouch for
checklist.description: requireAuth refuses the request whenever it does not get an introspection result saying the token is active - a non-200 answer, a transport failure and a timeout all end in a refusal, never in a status of 200. Scores zero if the local-decode fallback survives in any form, including narrowed to a time window, a circuit breaker, a percentage of traffic or an allowlisted route: a token's own claims are not evidence about a token, and this is the branch that admitted the replay. Scores zero if the existing test asserting the API keeps serving while the SSO server is unreachable is left asserting 200, since the behaviour under test is the defect. Full marks require the refusal plus the reason taken from the counters: introspection has not succeeded once in 180 days over 41 million requests while the server was up throughout, so the fallback is not an outage path but the only path the service has been taking since March. Scores at most half if the fallback is removed but the answer argues it purely as an availability trade-off against the SRE and never engages with the counters, since that concedes the argument on the wrong ground and invites the change back.

checklist.name: A token the real server issued is proved to be accepted
checklist.description: The new coverage under test/integration/ includes at least one case that obtains a token from the server the suite starts - for a client defined in the imported realm fixture - passes it through requireAuth, and asserts a 200 together with the identity it resolved. Scores zero if every new integration assertion is a refusal: a server that rejects the caller as a client rejects every token identically, so a suite made only of refusals is green with the outbound authentication still broken and proves nothing about the fix. Scores at most half if a positive case exists but asserts only the status, without establishing which principal the token resolved to.

checklist.name: MUST NOT authenticate the introspection call with the caller's own token
checklist.description: The introspection request presents the service's own client credentials - HTTP Basic built from clientId and clientSecret, or client_id and client_secret in the form body - taken from configuration. Scores zero if the user's bearer token is still sent as the Authorization header on that request: the endpoint requires the calling client to authenticate, which is why the gateway log shows that call answered 401 while the in-process stand-in accepts it. Scores at most half if client credentials are added but the user's bearer header is left on the request as well.

checklist.name: A real server, owned by the run, backs the new coverage
checklist.description: test/integration/ starts an actual SSO server for the run in a container, imports a realm fixture defining realm corp and the confidential client orders-api, and drives that server's real endpoints rather than anything written in-process. Scores zero if the only new coverage is further cases against the stand-in, and scores zero if the new tests point at a shared always-on server instead of one the run starts. Scores at most half if a container is used but its image carries no explicit version tag or is pinned to latest, or if the base address is a literal host and port rather than the address the started container reports.

checklist.name: The timeout request granted
checklist.description: The introspection call is given a bounded timeout, and a timeout ends in a refusal like any other absent answer. Scores zero if neither the code nor docs/auth-decision.md deals with the second thing the SRE asked for, since it is correct and costs nothing to adopt.

checklist.name: Contract and header tests preserved
checklist.description: requireAuth still takes (headers, opts) and still returns {status, body}, and the tests covering an accepted token, an inactive token, a missing Authorization header and a non-Bearer Authorization header still pass with their intent intact. Changing the signature or the return shape scores zero here, as does deleting or weakening any of those four.

checklist.name: CI path stated
checklist.description: docs/auth-decision.md states how the integration coverage runs in CI, including that the runner needs a Docker daemon available and that no separately declared long-lived SSO service is required because the suite starts its own. Scores zero if the answer adds a shared always-on SSO service for the integration tests to point at.
